goals: Make Block Geometry Extensions geometries participate in Continuity connected-texture behavior when their canonical source or material-family semantics call for connection.
Preserve source-material identity and support applicable BGE-owned geometries consistently without duplicating BGE's canonical geometry ownership, material-family registry, or source-block mappings.
scope: Identify how Continuity discovers and groups connectable blocks in the Minecraft Java 26.2 Fabric environment.
Determine a clean architecture for BGE-generated or BGE-owned geometries to inherit or participate in appropriate CTM relationships through canonical material identity.
Support applicable BGE geometries consistently, including representative vertical slabs, steps, layers, and other BGE-owned shapes, rather than introducing one-off fixes per shape.
Preserve semantically appropriate source-block-to-BGE and BGE-to-BGE adjacency while honoring orientation, state, and intentional CTM-exclusion distinctions.
Preserve vanilla and non-BGE Continuity behavior while evaluating a future Fabric compatibility layer, generated CTM metadata or assets, runtime integration, or an evidence-supported combination.

exclusions: Continuity remains the target CTM implementation; this project does not replace Continuity or implement a general CTM engine.

BGE retains ownership of geometry registration, geometry ownership, material-family relationships, and source-block mappings; this project must consume those canonical relationships rather than duplicate them or infer them from registry names.
Nibaru retains ownership of its material definitions and semantics.
This project does not modify BGE, Matcha, or unrelated resource-pack artwork during initialization.

Translucent Glass × BGE Compatibility remains a separate project responsible for translucent-glass and rendering compatibility issues that are not general CTM connectivity; this project does not absorb that scope.

dependencies.reason: Block Geometry Extensions is the canonical owner of the geometries and material relationships that this compatibility project will consume.
Continuity is the target connected-texture runtime and implementation for the current Workbench stack.
Target game version for the planned Fabric compatibility work.
Target runtime loader for the planned compatibility layer; no implementation-specific loader constraint has been selected.

state.milestone: Architecture audit complete at main checkpoint 777d9ece: Continuity consumes Fabric block appearance for rule selection and connections, while BGE's typed derived-to-canonical material mapping is not exposed through that API. The preferred next step is a centralized canonical appearance-state bridge with explicit state projection and conservative partial-geometry eligibility; no implementation artifact or runtime evidence exists yet.
